# Jubilees Chapter 24 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Isaac at the Wells; Esau Sells the Birthright

---

**24:1** And it came-to-pass after the death of Abraham that the LORD blessed his son Isaac, and Isaac arose from Hebron and went and dwelt at the well of the vision in the first year of the third week of the forty-third jubilee.

**24:2** And in the first year of the fourth week a famine began in the land besides the first famine, which had been in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went to the king of the Philistines to Gerar.

**24:3** And the LORD appeared to him and said: "Do not go down into Egypt; dwell in the land that I tell you, and sojourn in this land, and I will be with you and bless you. For I will give all these lands to you and to your seed, and I will establish the oath which I swore to Abraham your father, and will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven, and as the sand which is upon the seashore.

**24:4** And your seed shall inherit all these lands, and all the nations of the earth shall bless themselves by your seed. Because Abraham obeyed my voice and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws."

**24:5** And Isaac dwelt in Gerar three weeks of years.

**24:6** And Abimelech, the king of the Philistines, commanded regarding Isaac, saying: "He is my brother," for he feared to kill him on account of his wife Rebekah, for she was beautiful.

**24:7** And Isaac became strong among the Philistines and he had many possessions: flocks of sheep and herds of cattle and asses. And Isaac sowed in the land of the Philistines and he found a hundredfold, and Isaac became very great and the Philistines envied him.

**24:8** Now all the wells which Abraham's servants had dug during the lifetime of Abraham, the Philistines had stopped them up after the death of Abraham, and filled them with earth.

**24:9** And Abimelech said to Isaac: "Go away from us, for you have become much greater than we." And Isaac departed from there in the first year of the seventh week, and he sojourned in the valleys of Gerar.

**24:10** And they dug again the wells of water which Abraham's servants had dug during the lifetime of Abraham and which the Philistines had stopped up after the death of Abraham. And they called their names as Abraham his father had called them.

**24:11** And the servants of Isaac dug a well in the valley, and they found living water there. And the herdsmen of Gerar strove with the herdsmen of Isaac, saying: "The water is ours." And Isaac called the name of that well Contention, for they had contended with us.

**24:12** And they dug another well and they contended over it also. And Isaac called its name Enmity.

**24:13** And he moved away from there and dug another well, and they contended not over it. And Isaac called its name Spaciousness, and said: "For now the LORD has made room for us, and we have increased in the land."

**24:14** And he went up from there to the well of the oath in the second year of the seventh week.

**24:15** And the LORD appeared to him that night and said to him: "I am the God of Abraham your father. Fear not, for I am with you, and will bless you and will multiply your seed for the sake of Abraham my servant."

**24:16** And Isaac built there an altar and he called upon the name of the LORD. And he pitched his tent there, and there the servants of Isaac dug a well.

**24:17** And on that day the servants of Abimelech came to Isaac and said to him: "Let there be an oath between us: between us and you, and let us make a covenant with you, just as we did not touch you, and just as we did only good to you and we sent you away in peace. And now you are blessed by the LORD."

**24:18** And Isaac answered and said to them: "Why do you come to me, for you hate me and you sent me away from you?" And they said: "We clearly see that the LORD is with you, and we said: 'Let there now be an oath between us, between us and you, and let us make a covenant with you, that you will not do us evil, as we have not touched you and have not harmed you, but have done good to you and sent you away in peace. Now you are blessed of the LORD.'"

**24:19** And Isaac made a feast for them and they ate and drank and went away. And on that day they swore to each other. And Isaac sent them away and they departed from him in peace.

**24:20** And it came-to-pass on the same day that Esau came from the field hungry. And Esau said to Jacob his brother: "Give me of that red pottage." And Jacob said to his brother: "Sell to me your birthright this day."

**24:21** And Esau said: "I am going to die; what is this birthright to me?" And Jacob said: "Swear to me this day." And he swore to him and sold his birthright to Jacob.

**24:22** And Jacob gave to his brother Esau bread and lentil pottage, and he ate and drank and arose and went his way, and Esau despised his birthright.

**24:23** And in the seventh week in the first year thereof, Isaac sowed in the land of the Philistines, and he found a hundred measures, and Isaac became great and kept becoming greater and greater until he became very great.

**24:24** And in the second year of the seventh week a famine was in all the land except for the land of the Philistines.

**24:25** And the Philistines were jealous of Isaac's flocks and his herds and his possessions.

**24:26** And Abimelech, the king of the Philistines, said: "Be-it-known that everything that is yours is ours, and go hence from our land."

**24:27** And Isaac went from there to the valley and dug the wells anew.

**24:28** And all these things happened in those days.

---
*EMET notes: "Living water" (v.11) = mayim ḥayyim, running/spring water as opposed to cistern water. Well-names: Contention (Esek), Enmity (Sitnah), Spaciousness (Rehoboth) — cf. Gen 26:20-22. The birthright transaction (vv.20-22) is integrated here into the Isaac well-narrative, unlike Gen 25 where it stands alone.*
